passage:
I'm Rekha, and last winter I matched with someone called Nikhil on a dating app. Architect, dog lover, perfect grammar. Within a week he was saying he had never felt this way.
My friend Sonali had drilled three rules into me after her cousin lost savings to a fake profile: video call early, check the photos, never send money or private pictures to someone you haven't met.
So on day eight I said, "Quick video call tonight? Five minutes." He said his camera was broken. While we chatted, I ran his photos through a reverse image search. They belonged to a travel blogger in Portugal.
I didn't accuse him. I just said, "I'd love to keep talking, but only after a live call." The replies turned sharp: "You don't trust me? After everything?" Then he unmatched.
I reported the profile. It stung for a day. Then I felt proud. A real person would simply have turned on the camera.

qa.q: Whose photos did the reverse image search find?
qa.a: The photos belonged to a travel blogger in Portugal.

qa.q: How did Rekha feel after Nikhil unmatched?
qa.a: It stung for a day, and then Rekha felt proud for sticking to the checks.

qa.q: Which check revealed the most, and why?
qa.a: The reverse image search showed the photos were someone else's, and the calm request for a live call drew out anger instead of acceptance, which a real person would not show.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel hearing Rekha's story?
qa.a: Sonali would likely feel relieved and glad the rules helped, especially after seeing a cousin lose savings to a fake profile.

grounding: A person insists on an early live video call, reverse-searches the photos and refuses to send money or pictures, and the fake match reacts with anger.

passage:
Note from Siddharth, IT support lead, Friday.
Jomon came to my desk at lunch with his phone and a question: "Can you look at this with me before I do anything?"
For three weeks he had been chatting with "Anjali", who said she was a nurse abroad. Today she asked for gift cards to cover a stuck visa fee. Before coming to me, Jomon had already done three things: asked for a live video call (she said the hospital blocks cameras), run her photo through a reverse image search (it matched a model's page), and refused to send any money or photos.
He asked if he was being paranoid. I told him no, these were exactly the right checks, and a real person would not get angry at them. "Anjali" did.
Next steps: helped him report the profile to the app and file a complaint on the cybercrime portal. Suggested he share his three checks at Monday's team meeting.

qa.q: What did Anjali say she was?
qa.a: She said she was a nurse abroad.

qa.q: What was Jomon worried about when he came to the desk?
qa.a: He worried he was being paranoid and wanted a second opinion before doing anything.

qa.q: How did Siddharth support Jomon?
qa.a: Siddharth confirmed the checks were right, helped report the profile to the app and file a cybercrime complaint, and suggested Jomon share the checks with the team.

qa.q: What would change if Jomon had skipped the checks?
qa.a: He might have bought the gift cards and lost money, and the anger at his request for a call would not have stood out as a warning.

grounding: A supervisor records how Jomon insisted on a live call, reverse-searched a photo and refused to send money, and how together they reported the fake profile.

passage:
Saturday night
I did what Farida told me to do, and I'm so glad.
"Kabir" and I matched on the dating app two weeks ago. Perfect photos, perfect messages. An architect in Dubai. He said I was the most beautiful woman he'd ever spoken to.
Farida said, "Before you get any deeper, video call. Early. And do an image search." So on Thursday I asked for a quick video call. He said his camera was broken. Friday, I asked again. He got angry. "Don't you trust me? After everything?"
That anger was the answer, really. Farida sat with me while I did a reverse image search. His photos belonged to a fitness model in Brazil.
Tonight he asked me to send a "private" photo to prove I trust him. I blocked and reported him instead.
I'm sad. I liked those messages. But a real person would have just switched on the camera.
Ayesha

qa.q: Where did Kabir's photos actually come from?
qa.a: His photos belonged to a fitness model in Brazil.

qa.q: How does Ayesha feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Ayesha feels sad, having liked his messages, but also relieved and glad she followed Farida's advice.

qa.q: What checks protected Ayesha?
qa.a: Asking for an early video call, doing a reverse image search, and refusing to send a private photo, then blocking and reporting him.

qa.q: What does Kabir's anger at the video call request suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he was hiding something, because a real person would accept a simple check without anger.

grounding: A diary shows an adult insisting on an early video call and image search, refusing private images, and seeing anger at checks as a warning.

passage:
In the small town of Sagar, Sachin had been messaging a woman from a matrimonial site for three weeks. She said she worked as a nurse in London. She sent sweet messages every morning.
On Sunday, sitting on the steps of their house, he showed his cousin Nandini the latest message. "She's sending me a gold watch as a gift. But there's a customs fee. She says I need to pay ₹25,000 to the courier."
Nandini put down her tea. "Have you ever seen her on video?"
"Her camera doesn't work in the hospital."
"Let's check something." She did an image search on her phone. The photos belonged to a news reader from another country.
Sachin felt his face go hot. Then he took the phone back and typed, "Please do a video call first." The reply came fast: "You don't trust me? I'm hurt."
He blocked the profile and, with Nandini, reported it to the site that evening.

qa.q: How much did the woman say Sachin had to pay the courier?
qa.a: ₹25,000 to the courier.

qa.q: How did Sachin feel when the image search showed the truth?
qa.a: Sachin felt embarrassed, his face going hot, and then determined to test her with a video call request.

qa.q: What checks protected Sachin?
qa.a: An image search, asking for a video call first, and refusing to pay the customs fee, then blocking and reporting the profile.

qa.q: What does the woman's reply to the video call request suggest?
qa.a: Her hurt, angry reply suggests she was not real, since a genuine person would accept a simple video call.

grounding: It shows an adult insisting on a video call, doing an image search and refusing to send money to someone never met.

passage: Three days after matching with Chidi on a dating app in Manchester, Nour typed the message she had practised with her flatmate: "Before we chat more, can we do a quick video call? I do this with everyone." Earlier she had run his photos through an image search; they led only back to his own profile and a five-a-side football club page. Still, she waited for his reply with her thumb hovering over the block button. "Sure! Tonight at 8? Warning, my kitchen is a mess." At eight, there he was, real, laughing, a pan of jollof rice burning behind him. They talked for twenty minutes. Afterwards Nour texted her flatmate: "He's real, and he didn't mind at all." Her last match had sulked for days at the same question and then asked for help with "a customs fee". Nour had blocked that one. Her line stayed simple: no money and no private photos to anyone she had not met.

qa.q: Where did Nour's image search of Chidi's photos lead?
qa.a: Only back to his own profile and a five-a-side football club page.

qa.q: How was Nour feeling while waiting for Chidi's reply?
qa.a: Nour felt cautious and a little tense, thumb hovering over the block button in case he refused.

qa.q: Which of Nour's checks worked, and why?
qa.a: The image search and the early video call tested whether Chidi was real; his easy yes, unlike the last match's sulking and fee request, showed the difference.

qa.q: How might Chidi have seen the video-call request?
qa.a: Chidi seemed relaxed and even amused, joking about his messy kitchen, which suggests he saw it as a normal, fair check.

grounding: Shows a person asking for an early live video call and checking photos, and a genuine match accepting the checks without anger.
